title: Order of the Sinking Star Demo Highlights Early Contender for Game of the Year
text:
The puzzle adventure Order of the Sinking Star, designed by Jonathan David Blow, is available as a free demo during Steam Next Fest. The demo features over 100 puzzles and 110 levels, with more content arriving on June 19. The full game aims to include over 1,000 puzzles and is expected to launch later in 2026.
With only half of 2026 already gone, the gaming community is already buzzing with early predictions for the upcoming Game of the Year honors, and one title generating significant excitement is currently available as a free demo on Steam.
The Steam Next Fest is in full swing, offering over 5,000 free demos amounting to more than 90 days of total playtime. Amidst this vast library, one puzzle adventure stands out: Order of the Sinking Star from Arc Games. This is not a game for those seeking instant gratification; it is a deliberate, cerebral journey through a web of clever, interconnected riddles that build toward a grand mystery.
The game is crafted by renowned designer Jonathan David Blow, celebrated for his work on Braid and The Witness, and his signature brilliance is evident in every meticulously crafted corner of this experience. The demo already features more than 100 puzzles, with a substantial content update scheduled for June 19 that will add even more. The full version promises over 1,000 puzzles, meaning the demo only provides a tantalizing glimpse.
Beyond its core puzzle-solving, the game invites players to explore multiple distinct worlds, assume control of unique characters, and master mechanics that evolve throughout the adventure. The current demo includes 110 levels and an overworld linking three base worlds, with additional content on the way. It is a strictly single-player experience, so you won't be able to co-op with friends, but you can certainly share your most triumphant solving moments or challenge them to beat your times.
To try it, simply search for Order of the Sinking Star on Steam and install the demo from its store page. The demo will be accessible until June 22, and any progress you make will transfer to the full game when it launches. While an official release date hasn't been set, the game is expected later this year, and adding it to your wishlist ensures you'll get notified.
The game is also compatible with Steam Deck, though it hasn't yet received the official "Verified" badge; developers are committed to optimization and aim to secure verification before launch. For those without a powerful PC, the demo is also playable via NVIDIA GeForce NOW. One note on the demo: it uses placeholder computer-generated voiceover narration, a temporary measure that will be replaced with professional voice acting for the final release.
This AI-generated element is confined to the demo and will not appear in the finished product. Steam, the platform hosting this event, was originally released on September 12, 2003, and continues to be a central hub for PC gaming
